answer: A winter fur post on a braided river delta used to let one clerk mint extra lot tickets and cash the same pelt twice. A trapper may now occupy only one surveyed ice cell, hang a 38 cm sable hide whose ear-notch is photographed when a wild raven first lands on the weighing pole, and stake 9.7 coin plus a 410 g iron tally in the locker for 21 hours. Two stewards rematch the ear-notch, the locker seal, and three wet-weight tickets 11 minutes apart within 8 meters of the pole. If two tickets share one cell pin or one tally mass, both stakes burn and that cell stays shut for seven nights.
